items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove stale classifier-model guidance**

This line still directs Codex users to configure a separately pinned permgate classifier model, while the newly changed rule at line 55 says no classifier runs and the commit deletes those policy fields. This makes the installed `AGENTS.md` self-contradictory and can lead users to add a meaningless classifier setting to the security policy; remove the obsolete sentence when making permgate deterministic-only.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/f26975abde8aa161569a1d96cff5021c31d75c0b/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-object permgate policy files**

A JSON array such as `["schema_version", "allow_patterns", "deny_patterns"]` satisfies `set(policy)` and therefore passes this asset check, but the installed executable then raises an unhandled `AttributeError` on `policy.get(...)`, exits 1, and writes no decision log. Require a mapping and validate `schema_version == 3` here so a malformed policy cannot pass validation and be deployed to the PermissionRequest hook.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate policy pattern entries before returning**

With a policy such as `{"schema_version":3,"allow_patterns":[null],"deny_patterns":[]}`, the new top-level-only validation accepts the file and this function returns it. `decide()` then calls `pattern.get(...)` on the null entry, raising an uncaught `AttributeError`; the hook exits 1 without the intended fail-closed `config-error` record or decision log. Validate the pattern arrays and their entries here (or catch `AttributeError`) so malformed policy content falls through safely.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
